question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

You know that I am fond of reading / and also that all books are my favourite / but you don't know that this is one of / my favourite book.
option_1: but you don't know that this is one of
option_2: and also that all books are my favourite
option_4: You know that I am fond of reading
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. my favourite book.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The structure "one of + the/my + plural noun" always takes a plural noun. After "this is one of my favourite ___", the noun must be plural, so it should be "my favourite books", not "my favourite book".

◦ Correct: ... but you don't know that this is one of my favourite books.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• The other segments — "You know that I am fond of reading", "and also that all books are my favourite" and "but you don't know that this is one of" — are grammatically correct.

NOTE

• Rule: one of / each of / none of / either of + plural noun (one of my friends, one of the books). The verb, however, agrees with "one" and stays singular (One of my friends is here).

question:
Select the option that correctly rectifies the underlined spelling error.

The worlds you and I belong to are very defferent.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. different.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "different", meaning not the same; unlike. (भिन्न / अलग)

◦ Correct: The worlds you and I belong to are very different.

• Spelling key: DIF + FER + ENT.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "deffirent", "diferent" and "deferent" are all misspellings of "different". ("Deferent" is a rare word meaning respectful/submissive, but it does not fit the sentence and is not the intended correction.)

NOTE

• Related words: difference (noun), differ (verb), differently (adverb). Watch the double "f" and single "r".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Vague
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Indefinite.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Vague" means not clear, uncertain or not precisely defined. Its closest synonym is "indefinite" (not clearly fixed or defined). (अस्पष्ट / अनिश्चित)

◦ Example: He gave only a vague/indefinite answer about his plans.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Dissimilar" (unlike) and Option 2 "Distinct" (clearly different/clear) are not synonyms — "distinct" is actually the opposite of vague.

• Option 4 "Intact" (whole, undamaged) is unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of vague: unclear, hazy, indefinite, ambiguous, obscure. Antonyms: clear, definite, distinct, precise.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

He is the healthy person I have ever met in life.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. healthiest.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "the ... I have ever met" signals the superlative degree. The superlative of "healthy" is "healthiest".

◦ Correct: He is the healthiest person I have ever met in life.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "healthy" is a short adjective, so it forms degrees by adding -ier / -iest (healthy – healthier – healthiest), not with "more/most".

• Option 1 "most healthy" and Option 2 "more healthy" are non-standard double/wrong forms; Option 3 "healthier" (comparative) does not fit "the ... ever".

NOTE

• Structure "one of / the + superlative ... that I have ever + V3" always needs the superlative: the best film I have ever seen, the healthiest person I have ever met.

question: Select the grammatically correct sentence from the options given.
option_1: Neither the boy nor the mother could identify the man.
option_2: Neither the boy nor a mother could identify a man.
option_3: Neither a boy nor a mother could identify the man.
option_4: Neither a boy nor the mother could identify a man.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Neither the boy nor the mother could identify the man.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Both "boy" and "mother" refer to specific, known persons, so each needs the definite article "the". Likewise "the man" is a specific person. Option 1 uses "the" consistently and correctly.

◦ Correct: Neither the boy nor the mother could identify the man.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2, 3 and 4 mix "a" and "the" inconsistently, wrongly making a specific, already-referred person indefinite.

NOTE

• "Neither ... nor" is a correlative conjunction. The verb agrees with the nearer subject (proximity rule): "Neither the boys nor the mother is here".

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Fluctuate
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Steady.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Fluctuate" means to change or vary irregularly; to rise and fall. Its antonym is "steady", meaning firm, stable and unchanging. (उतार-चढ़ाव होना का विलोम — स्थिर)

◦ Example: Prices that fluctuate are unstable, while steady prices remain constant.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Descend" (to go down) and Option 3 "Mitigate" (to lessen/ease) are unrelated.

• Option 4 "Wobble" (to shake unsteadily) is closer to a synonym of fluctuate.

NOTE

• Synonyms of fluctuate: vary, waver, oscillate, swing. Antonyms: steady, stabilise, remain constant.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

I could make out from my son's voice that he was _____ as his exam did not go well.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. sad.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The clause "as his exam did not go well" gives the reason for a low mood, so the blank needs "sad" (unhappy). (उदास / दुखी)

◦ Correct: I could make out from my son's voice that he was sad as his exam did not go well.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "abrogated" (to abolish/repeal a law) and Option 4 "rejected" (refused) describe things, not a person's mood here.

• Option 2 "confused" (puzzled) does not fit "his exam did not go well" as well as "sad".

NOTE

• Adjectives of emotion: sad, gloomy, dejected, downcast, disheartened. "Make out" here means to understand/perceive.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

The space or room that is at the top of a building or just below the main roof
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Attic.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An "attic" is a room or space at the top of a building, just under the roof, often used for storage. (अटारी / छत के नीचे का कमरा)

◦ Example: They stored old boxes in the attic.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Dome" (a rounded roof), Option 2 "Ceiling" (the inner upper surface of a room) and Option 3 "Stairs" (steps between floors) do not mean a top-floor room.

NOTE

• Related terms: loft (a similar space under the roof), basement/cellar (a room below ground level), garret (a small, often dingy attic room).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Extensive
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Limited.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Extensive" means large in area, scope or amount; wide-ranging. Its antonym is "limited", meaning small, restricted or narrow. (विस्तृत का विलोम — सीमित)

◦ Example: He has extensive knowledge, while she has only limited experience.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Abstract" (not concrete) and Option 4 "Concrete" (solid/real) are opposites of each other, not of "extensive".

• Option 3 "Expensive" (costly) sounds similar to "extensive" but is unrelated in meaning.

NOTE

• Synonyms of extensive: vast, wide, comprehensive, broad. Antonyms: limited, narrow, restricted, confined.

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.

Getting a sudden promotion and increment in my current profile was like _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. a bolt from the blue.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "a bolt from the blue" means a sudden, unexpected event or surprise. A "sudden promotion and increment" being unexpected fits this idiom. (अप्रत्याशित घटना)

◦ Example: The news of his resignation came like a bolt from the blue.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "a fish out of water" (someone uncomfortable in an unfamiliar situation), Option 3 "a ballpark figure" (a rough estimate) and Option 4 "a foul play" (unfair/criminal behaviour) do not fit.

NOTE

• Similar idioms of surprise: "out of the blue", "caught off guard", "a rude shock".

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Once in a blue moon
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. A rare occurrence.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "once in a blue moon" means very rarely; hardly ever. (कभी-कभार / बहुत कम)

◦ Example: He visits his village only once in a blue moon.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "A regular activity" and 2 "A frequent event" are the opposite of the idiom's meaning.

• Option 4 "A pleasant surprise" is unrelated.

NOTE

• Idioms of rarity/frequency: "once in a blue moon" (rarely), "every now and then" (occasionally), "day in, day out" (constantly).

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

Chetan's room is clean / than Ram's room because / Chetan cleans it more often than Ram.
option_1: Chetan cleans it more often than Ram
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Chetan's room is clean.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "than" (in the next segment) requires the comparative degree. So "clean" must become "cleaner". The error lies in the segment "Chetan's room is clean".

◦ Correct: Chetan's room is cleaner than Ram's room because Chetan cleans it more often than Ram.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "than Ram's room because" and "Chetan cleans it more often than Ram" are correct.

NOTE

• Comparative degree is used with "than": cleaner than, taller than, more careful than. Positive "clean" cannot go with "than".

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.

Stephan, however, contrived / to put away / his departure / for eighteen months.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. to put away.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct phrasal verb here is "to put off", meaning to postpone/delay. "Put away" means to store something, which does not fit "his departure". The error is in "to put away".

◦ Correct: Stephan, however, contrived to put off his departure for eighteen months.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "contrived" (managed/planned cleverly), "his departure" and "for eighteen months" are all correct.

NOTE

• Phrasal verbs with "put": put off (postpone), put away (store), put up with (tolerate), put out (extinguish), put down (suppress/write).

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

Her decision, / given the complex circumstances, / was too impulsively made.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. was too impulsively made.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Too" carries a negative sense of "excessively". A decision described neutrally should use "very/rather impulsively made" or simply "impulsively made". The misuse of "too" here makes the segment "was too impulsively made" the error.

◦ Correct: Her decision, given the complex circumstances, was rather impulsively made / very impulsively made.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Her decision," and "given the complex circumstances," are correct.

NOTE

• "Too" means "more than enough" and usually implies a bad result (too hot to drink). For simple emphasis use "very/rather".

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Supperannuation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Supperannuation" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "superannuation", meaning a regular payment/pension made to a person after retirement. (सेवानिवृत्ति पेंशन)

◦ Spelling key: SUPER + ANNU + ATION.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Phytoplankton" (microscopic aquatic plants), "Accentuation" (the act of emphasising) and "Suppressant" (something that suppresses) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• "Superannuation" comes from Latin "super" (beyond) + "annus" (year). Note the single "p" and double "n".

question:
Select the option with the correct spelling to replace the underlined word in the given sentence.

Development does not take place in a vaccum.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. vacuum.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "vacuum", meaning a space entirely empty of matter; an absence of surroundings/context. (निर्वात / रिक्तता)

◦ Correct: Development does not take place in a vacuum.

• Spelling key: VAC + U + UM (single "c", double "u").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "vaccum", "vacuuem", "vakum" and "vaccim" are all misspellings.

NOTE

• "Does not take place in a vacuum" is an idiom meaning it does not happen in isolation. "Vacuum" is one of the few English words with a double "u".

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

We can observed from the poll that the award is likely to go to the horror movie director this year.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. can observe from.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After the modal verb "can", the base form (V1) of the verb is used, i.e., "observe", not "observed". The correct preposition with "observe" here is "from".

◦ Correct: We can observe from the poll that the award is likely to go to ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2 "have been observing of" and 3 "are observing of" use the wrong preposition "of".

• Option 4 "had observe from" wrongly uses base form after "had" (it needs V3, "observed").

NOTE

• Modal verbs (can, could, will, shall, may, must, should) are always followed by the base form of the main verb: can go, must see, should observe.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Amplify
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Contract.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Amplify" means to increase, enlarge or make louder/stronger. Its antonym is "contract", meaning to make or become smaller/shorter. (विस्तार करना का विलोम — सिकुड़ना)

◦ Example: A microphone amplifies sound, whereas cold contracts metal.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Enlarge" is a synonym of amplify.

• Option 3 "Exert" (to apply/use effort) and Option 4 "Defy" (to resist) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of amplify: magnify, expand, intensify, boost. Antonyms: contract, reduce, diminish, lessen.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Expand
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Shrink.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Expand" means to grow larger; to increase in size or extent. Its antonym is "shrink", meaning to become smaller. (फैलना का विलोम — सिकुड़ना)

◦ Example: Metals expand on heating and shrink/contract on cooling.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Inflate" (to swell/fill with air) is a near synonym of expand.

• Options 2 "Protect" (to guard) and 4 "Network" (to connect) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of expand: enlarge, grow, extend, swell. Antonyms: shrink, contract, compress, condense.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.

Our ______ has so many magnificent tourist destinations, with unimaginable potential, yet to ____ fully explored.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. country; be.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The first blank needs a singular noun as the subject — "country" fits ("Our country has ...").

• The second blank follows "yet to", which requires the base form "be" in the passive structure "yet to be fully explored".

◦ Correct: Our country has so many magnificent tourist destinations, with unimaginable potential, yet to be fully explored.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "national" is an adjective, not a noun, so it cannot be the subject.

• "yet to been/have/has explored" are grammatically wrong; only "yet to be explored" is correct.

NOTE

• "yet to be + past participle" is a passive structure meaning "not done so far": yet to be decided, yet to be announced, yet to be explored.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

She went on a quest for ancient things ___(1)____ could have a soul of their own, something ___(2)___ Aladdin's lamp that was home to a genie. She searched flea markets, met with art dealers and even went to excavation sites. She ___(3)__ searching for something that would have seen some ancient history when an ___(4)___, ___(5)___, ___(6)____ apothecary table caught her attention. It was perhaps owned by a __(7)____, ___(8)___, __(9)____ woman who was a wise medic but was deemed a witch.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. that.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank refers to "ancient things" (non-living objects). The relative pronoun "that" correctly introduces the defining relative clause describing these things.

◦ Correct: She went on a quest for ancient things that could have a soul of their own ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "who" is used only for people, so it cannot refer to "things".

• "whose" shows possession, and "which" is possible but "that" is the best fit for this defining clause about things.

NOTE

• Relative pronouns: who (people), which/that (things/animals), whose (possession), whom (object — people).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

She went on a quest for ancient things ___(1)____ could have a soul of their own, something ___(2)___ Aladdin's lamp that was home to a genie. She searched flea markets, met with art dealers and even went to excavation sites. She ___(3)__ searching for something that would have seen some ancient history when an ___(4)___, ___(5)___, ___(6)____ apothecary table caught her attention. It was perhaps owned by a __(7)____, ___(8)___, __(9)____ woman who was a wise medic but was deemed a witch.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. like.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence draws a comparison — "something like Aladdin's lamp" means "something similar to Aladdin's lamp". The preposition "like" (meaning "similar to") fits.

◦ Correct: ... something like Aladdin's lamp that was home to a genie.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "of", Option 3 "upstairs" and Option 4 "by" do not convey the intended comparison and break the sense.

NOTE

• "Like" as a preposition = "similar to / such as" (a fruit like a mango). Do not confuse with "as", which is used before a clause (do as I say).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

She went on a quest for ancient things ___(1)____ could have a soul of their own, something ___(2)___ Aladdin's lamp that was home to a genie. She searched flea markets, met with art dealers and even went to excavation sites. She ___(3)__ searching for something that would have seen some ancient history when an ___(4)___, ___(5)___, ___(6)____ apothecary table caught her attention. It was perhaps owned by a __(7)____, ___(8)___, __(9)____ woman who was a wise medic but was deemed a witch.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. was.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage is written in the past tense (searched, went, caught) and the subject "She" is singular. The past continuous "was searching" fits: "She was searching for something ...".

◦ Correct: She was searching for something that would have seen some ancient history ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "were" is plural and does not agree with the singular "She".

• Options 2 "has been" and 4 "is" are present-tense forms that clash with the past-tense narrative.

NOTE

• Past continuous = was/were + verb-ing, used for an ongoing past action: "She was searching". With "She/he/it" use "was".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

She went on a quest for ancient things ___(1)____ could have a soul of their own, something ___(2)___ Aladdin's lamp that was home to a genie. She searched flea markets, met with art dealers and even went to excavation sites. She ___(3)__ searching for something that would have seen some ancient history when an ___(4)___, ___(5)___, ___(6)____ apothecary table caught her attention. It was perhaps owned by a __(7)____, ___(8)___, __(9)____ woman who was a wise medic but was deemed a witch.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blanks numbered 4, 5 and 6 respectively.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. antique; heavy; chestnut brown.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• English follows the Royal Order of Adjectives: opinion → size → age → shape → colour → origin → material → purpose. Here the natural order before "apothecary table" is age (antique) → size/quality (heavy) → colour (chestnut brown).

◦ Correct: ... an antique, heavy, chestnut brown apothecary table caught her attention.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 3 and 4 place the colour "chestnut brown" or "heavy" in the wrong position, breaking the standard adjective order.

NOTE

• Order of adjectives (mnemonic OSASCOMP): Opinion, Size, Age, Shape, Colour, Origin, Material, Purpose (e.g., "a lovely small old round brown Italian wooden table").

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

She went on a quest for ancient things ___(1)____ could have a soul of their own, something ___(2)___ Aladdin's lamp that was home to a genie. She searched flea markets, met with art dealers and even went to excavation sites. She ___(3)__ searching for something that would have seen some ancient history when an ___(4)___, ___(5)___, ___(6)____ apothecary table caught her attention. It was perhaps owned by a __(7)____, ___(8)___, __(9)____ woman who was a wise medic but was deemed a witch.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blanks numbered 7, 8 and 9 respectively.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. small; hunch-backed; old.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Following the Royal Order of Adjectives (size → shape → age), the sequence describing the "woman" is size (small) → shape (hunch-backed) → age (old).

◦ Correct: It was perhaps owned by a small, hunch-backed, old woman who was a wise medic ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• The other options disturb the size–shape–age order and therefore sound unnatural.

NOTE

• Order of adjectives (mnemonic OSASCOMP): Opinion, Size, Age, Shape, Colour, Origin, Material, Purpose. "Small" (size) usually comes before "hunch-backed" (shape) and "old" (age) as the tested pattern here.

question: The Indian Bureau of Mines (IBM) was established in the year ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1948.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Indian Bureau of Mines (IBM)" was established in 1948. It is a subordinate office under the Ministry of Mines, responsible for the conservation and scientific development of mineral resources (other than coal, petroleum, natural gas and atomic minerals). (भारतीय खान ब्यूरो — 1948)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The IBM's headquarters is at Nagpur, Maharashtra.

• It promotes systematic and scientific mining, mineral conservation and protection of the environment in mines.

NOTE

• Do not confuse with the Geological Survey of India (GSI), founded in 1851 at Kolkata, which handles geological surveys and mineral exploration.

question: Nife layer of earth is situated in the ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Core.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Nife" layer is situated in the Core of the Earth. The name comes from Ni (Nickel) + Fe (Ferrum/Iron), the main constituents of the innermost layer. (निफे — पृथ्वी का क्रोड़)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Earth has three main layers: the Crust (outermost), Mantle (SIMA/SIAL region) and Core (innermost, Nife).

• The crust is rich in Silica and Alumina (SIAL); the mantle in Silica and Magnesium (SIMA).

NOTE

• The Earth's core is divided into a liquid outer core and a solid inner core, and it is the source of the Earth's magnetic field.

question: Which of the following crops that spread to northern India in the early years of the 17th century was NOT mentioned in the Ain-i-Akbari in the lists of crops in northern India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tobacco.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Tobacco" spread to northern India only in the early 17th century and was therefore NOT mentioned in the Ain-i-Akbari (which was compiled earlier, in the 1590s). (तंबाकू — आइन-ए-अकबरी में उल्लेखित नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Ain-i-Akbari was written by Abul Fazl, Akbar's court historian, as the third volume of the Akbarnama. It gives detailed administrative, economic and agricultural information about Akbar's empire.

• Crops like wheat, arhar and jowar were already established staples of northern India and were listed in it.

NOTE

• Tobacco and other New World crops (like potato, maize, chilli and tomato) reached India through the Portuguese during the 16th–17th centuries.

question: Who among the following was the first Law and Justice Minister of independent India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is BR Ambedkar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Dr. B. R. Ambedkar was the first Law and Justice Minister of independent India (in Jawaharlal Nehru's first cabinet). (डॉ. बी. आर. अंबेडकर — प्रथम कानून मंत्री)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Dr. Ambedkar was also the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constitution of India and is known as the "Father of the Indian Constitution".

• He was posthumously awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1990.

NOTE

• John Matthai was an early Finance Minister; Jagjivan Ram was the first Labour Minister; Rajkumari Amrit Kaur was the first Health Minister of independent India.

question: Which of the following statements is/are correct according to the Census of India-2011? (a) A person aged seven years or above, who can both read and write with understanding in any language, is treated as literate. (b) A person who can only read but cannot write is not literate.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both (a) and (b) are correct.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Census of India 2011, a person aged seven years or above who can both read and write with understanding in any language is treated as literate. So statement (a) is correct.

• A person who can only read but cannot write is not counted as literate — so statement (b) is also correct. (जनगणना 2011 — साक्षरता की परिभाषा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Census 2011 was the 15th National Census and the 7th since independence.

• National literacy rate (2011) was about 74.04%; Kerala had the highest literacy and Bihar the lowest among the states.

NOTE

• The Census slogan for 2011 was "Our Census, Our Future". The census is conducted every 10 years by the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India (under the Ministry of Home Affairs).

question: In May 2023, Prime Minister Narendra Modi has been awarded the highest honours by the Pacific island nations of Papua New Guinea and ______________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fiji.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In May 2023, Prime Minister Narendra Modi was conferred the highest honours by the Pacific island nations of Papua New Guinea (the Grand Companion of the Order of Logohu) and Fiji (the Companion of the Order of Fiji). (फिजी और पापुआ न्यू गिनी के सर्वोच्च सम्मान)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• These honours were conferred around the third Forum for India–Pacific Islands Cooperation (FIPIC) Summit held in Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea.

• Fiji is an island nation in the South Pacific; its capital is Suva.

NOTE

• PM Modi has received several international honours, including Saudi Arabia's King Abdulaziz Sash, the UAE's Order of Zayed and Russia's Order of St Andrew.

question: Which of the following articles mentions about the Appropriation Bills in the state legislature?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 204.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 204 of the Constitution deals with Appropriation Bills in the state legislature — it provides that no money can be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of the State except under an Appropriation Act. (अनुच्छेद 204 — विनियोग विधेयक, राज्य विधानमंडल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Article 202 — Annual Financial Statement (state budget).

• Article 203 — Procedure in the legislature with respect to estimates.

• Article 207 — Special provisions as to financial Bills.

NOTE

• At the Union level, Appropriation Bills are dealt with under Article 114. Money Bills at the state level fall under Article 199.

question: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Function of President - France.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The pair "Function of President - France" is INCORRECTLY matched. India's provisions relating to the office/functions of the President (and the parliamentary system) are borrowed largely from Britain (the UK), not France. (भारत का राष्ट्रपति पद ब्रिटेन से प्रेरित)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Correctly matched borrowings: Rule of Law – Britain; Procedure Established by Law – Japan; Concurrent List – Australia.

• From France, India borrowed the ideals of Liberty, Equality and Fraternity and the concept of a Republic.

NOTE

• Other borrowings: Fundamental Rights & Judicial Review – USA; Directive Principles – Ireland; Emergency provisions – Germany; Fundamental Duties & Five-Year Plans – USSR; Federal structure – Canada.

question: Which of the following statements are correct about Ribosomes? Statement A: Ribosomes have no membrane. Statement B: Digestive hydrolytic enzymes are present in Ribosomes. Statement C: These are called suicidal bags. Statement D: Ribosomes play an important role in protein synthesis.
option_3: Only statements A, B and C
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only statements A and D.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Statement A is correct: Ribosomes have no membrane (they are non-membranous organelles made of RNA and protein).

• Statement D is correct: Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis (they are called the "protein factories" of the cell). (राइबोसोम — प्रोटीन संश्लेषण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Statements B and C actually describe lysosomes, which contain digestive hydrolytic enzymes and are called "suicidal bags" of the cell.

• Ribosomes may be free in the cytoplasm or attached to the rough endoplasmic reticulum.

NOTE

• Ribosomes were discovered by George Palade. They occur in both prokaryotic (70S) and eukaryotic (80S) cells.

question: 'Yakshagana', the famous folk dance, is associated with which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karnataka.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Yakshagana" is a traditional folk dance-drama theatre form of Karnataka, especially of the coastal (Malnad) regions. It combines dance, music, dialogue, elaborate costumes and make-up, usually depicting stories from the epics. (यक्षगान — कर्नाटक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Yakshagana performances are usually held at night and draw themes from the Ramayana and Mahabharata.

• Other folk/dance forms of Karnataka include Dollu Kunitha and Bayalata.

NOTE

• Famous folk dances: Bihu – Assam; Garba – Gujarat; Bhangra – Punjab; Chhau – Jharkhand/Odisha/West Bengal; Yakshagana – Karnataka.

question: The Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Protsahan Yojana (PMRPY) was launched by which Ministry of Government of India in the year 2016?
option_2: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ministry of Labour and Employment.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Protsahan Yojana (PMRPY)" was launched in 2016 by the Ministry of Labour and Employment. It aimed to incentivise employers to create new jobs by paying the employers' contribution (EPF/EPS) for new employees. (पीएमआरपीवाई — श्रम एवं रोजगार मंत्रालय)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Under PMRPY, the government paid the 8.33% EPS contribution (and later the full 12% EPF+EPS) of employers for eligible new employees.

• It was aimed at boosting formal-sector employment and bringing more workers under social security.

NOTE

• The scheme is implemented through the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO), which functions under the Ministry of Labour and Employment.

question: The College of Fort William was established at ______ under British rule.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Calcutta.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "College of Fort William" was established at Calcutta in 1800 by Lord Wellesley. It was set up to train British civil servants in Indian languages, laws, customs and administration. (फोर्ट विलियम कॉलेज — कलकत्ता, 1800)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The college became a major centre for the study and development of Indian languages (Bengali, Hindi, Urdu, Sanskrit, Persian, etc.).

• Scholars like William Carey were associated with it and contributed to the growth of modern Bengali and Hindi prose.

NOTE

• Fort William itself was a British fort in Calcutta. The city of Calcutta (Kolkata) was founded by Job Charnock of the East India Company.

question: Which of the following is a public sector industry in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL)" is a public sector (government-owned) industry in India. It is one of the largest steel-producing companies, under the Ministry of Steel. (सेल — सार्वजनिक क्षेत्र का उद्यम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• TISCO (now Tata Steel), Bajaj and Hindustan Unilever Limited (HUL) are all private sector companies.

• SAIL is a Maharatna company; it operates major integrated steel plants at Bhilai, Bokaro, Durgapur, Rourkela and Burnpur.

NOTE

• Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) are classified as Maharatna, Navratna and Miniratna based on their financial performance and autonomy.

question: What cellular structure is responsible for breaking down and recycling cellular components and molecules?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lysosome.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Lysosomes" are the cellular structures responsible for breaking down and recycling worn-out cellular components, waste materials and molecules. They contain powerful digestive (hydrolytic) enzymes. (लाइसोसोम — कोशिका की पाचन थैली)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Lysosomes are called the "suicidal bags" of the cell because they can digest the cell itself when it is damaged.

• They were discovered by Christian de Duve.

NOTE

• Ribosomes synthesise proteins; mitochondria are the "powerhouse of the cell" (produce ATP); the nucleus controls cell activities and stores DNA.

question: In tennis, what is a 'love' score?
option_1: The score when the game is tied
option_2: The highest possible score in a game
option_3: The score when a player has zero points
option_4: The score when a player wins the first point in a game
solution_text:
The correct answer is The score when a player has zero points.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In tennis, "love" means a score of zero (0) points. For example, "15–love" means one player has 15 and the other has 0. (टेनिस में 'लव' = शून्य अंक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The term "love" is believed to come from the French word "l'oeuf" (meaning "egg", which looks like a zero), or from the idea of playing "for love" (for nothing).

• Tennis point sequence: love (0) → 15 → 30 → 40 → game.

NOTE

• Other tennis terms: deuce (40–40), advantage, ace (an unreturnable serve), fault (a service error), and Grand Slams (Australian Open, French Open, Wimbledon, US Open).

question: Which city hosted the XXII Commonwealth Games 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Birmingham.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The XXII (22nd) Commonwealth Games 2022 were hosted by Birmingham, England (United Kingdom). (बर्मिंघम — राष्ट्रमंडल खेल 2022)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• India finished fourth in the medal tally at Birmingham 2022 with 61 medals (22 gold, 16 silver, 23 bronze).

• Australia topped the medal tally.

NOTE

• Commonwealth Games hosts: Delhi 2010, Glasgow 2014, Gold Coast 2018, Birmingham 2022. The next edition (2026) is to be held in Glasgow, Scotland. The Games are held every four years.

question: 'Getting A Grip: On My Body, My Mind, My Self' is an autobiography by who among the following tennis icons?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Monica Seles.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Getting A Grip: On My Body, My Mind, My Self" is the autobiography/memoir of the former World No. 1 tennis player Monica Seles. (मोनिका सेलेस की आत्मकथा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Monica Seles won nine Grand Slam singles titles and was once ranked World No. 1. She survived an on-court stabbing attack in 1993.

• She originally represented Yugoslavia and later the United States.

NOTE

• Tennis autobiographies: Open (Andre Agassi), Ace Against Odds (Sania Mirza), Unstoppable: My Life So Far (Maria Sharapova).

question: Who is the recipient of Padma Vibhushan 2000 for reviving the Odissi Classical dance form?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kelucharan Mohapatra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra received the Padma Vibhushan in 2000 for his pioneering role in reviving and popularising the Odissi classical dance form. (केलुचरण महापात्र — ओडिसी नृत्य)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• He was one of the greatest gurus of Odissi and trained many renowned dancers.

• He had earlier been awarded the Padma Shri (1974) and Padma Bhushan (1988).

NOTE

• Odissi is the classical dance of Odisha. Other Odissi exponents include Sanjukta Panigrahi and Sonal Mansingh.

question: Which of the following was the first subcontinental empire?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mauryan Empire.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Mauryan Empire" (founded by Chandragupta Maurya in 322 BCE) is considered the first subcontinental (pan-Indian) empire, as it unified almost the entire Indian subcontinent under one rule. (मौर्य साम्राज्य — प्रथम उपमहाद्वीपीय साम्राज्य)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Chandragupta Maurya was helped by his mentor Chanakya (Kautilya), author of the Arthashastra.

• Under Ashoka the Great, the empire reached its greatest extent; after the Kalinga War, Ashoka embraced Buddhism.

NOTE

• The Mauryan capital was Pataliputra. Megasthenes, a Greek ambassador, wrote "Indica" describing Mauryan India.

question: A molecule with the chemical formula C2H6 is a/an _______ molecule.
solution_text:
The correct answer is ethane.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A molecule with the chemical formula C₂H₆ is "ethane", the second member of the alkane (saturated hydrocarbon) series. (एथेन — C₂H₆)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Alkanes follow the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.

◦ Methane – CH₄ (n = 1)

◦ Ethane – C₂H₆ (n = 2)

◦ Propane – C₃H₈ (n = 3)

◦ Butane – C₄H₁₀ (n = 4)

NOTE

• Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with only single bonds. Methane (CH₄) is the main component of natural gas and a greenhouse gas; LPG is mainly butane and propane.

question: What are the three components of the empowerment model in SAPAP of SHGs?
option_1: Collective empowerment, capital formation, and poverty eradication
option_2: Public resource allocation, capacity building, and microfinance
option_3: Social mobilisation, capital formation, and capacity building
option_4: Social mobilisation, economic development, and education
solution_text:
The correct answer is Social mobilisation, capital formation, and capacity building.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The three components of the empowerment model in SAPAP (South Asia Poverty Alleviation Programme) of Self-Help Groups (SHGs) are Social mobilisation, Capital formation, and Capacity building. (सामाजिक गतिशीलता, पूँजी निर्माण और क्षमता निर्माण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Self-Help Groups (SHGs) are small voluntary associations, usually of women, formed to promote savings, mutual help and micro-credit.

• The SAPAP was supported by the UNDP and influenced later rural livelihood programmes in India.

NOTE

• In India, SHGs are linked to banks under the SHG-Bank Linkage Programme promoted by NABARD, helping in financial inclusion and women's empowerment.

question: The famous Qila-i-Kuhna (mosque of the old fort) was built by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sher Shah.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The famous "Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque" (inside the Purana Qila / Old Fort in Delhi) was built by Sher Shah Suri. It is a fine example of early Indo-Islamic (Afghan) architecture. (किला-ए-कुहना मस्जिद — शेर शाह सूरी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Sher Shah Suri (founder of the Sur Empire) defeated Humayun and ruled Delhi from 1540 to 1545.

• He is famous for his administrative reforms, the introduction of the rupiya (silver coin), and building/repairing the Grand Trunk (GT) Road.

NOTE

• The Purana Qila is believed to stand on the site of Indraprastha. Sher Shah also built his magnificent tomb at Sasaram (Bihar).

question: Which of the following states launched Mukhya Mantri Vriksh Sampada Yojana in March 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chhattisgarh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The state of Chhattisgarh launched the "Mukhya Mantri Vriksh Sampada Yojana" in March 2023. The scheme aims to promote tree plantation on private and community land, boost green cover and increase farmers' income. (मुख्यमंत्री वृक्ष संपदा योजना — छत्तीसगढ़)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The scheme encourages commercial plantation of trees and provides support to farmers and communities for afforestation.

• Chhattisgarh was carved out of Madhya Pradesh in 2000; its capital is Raipur.

NOTE

• Chhattisgarh, rich in forests and minerals, also runs schemes like the Godhan Nyay Yojana and Rajiv Gandhi Kisan Nyay Yojana.

question: In which of the following months is the Tuluni festival celebrated in Nagaland by the Sumi tribe?
solution_text:
The correct answer is July.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Tuluni festival" is celebrated in the month of July in Nagaland by the Sumi (Sema) tribe. It is a festival of feasting, marriage and merriment, marking the season of abundance. (तुलुनी उत्सव — नागालैंड, सुमी जनजाति)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Tuluni" refers to a drink made from rice, an important part of the celebration; the festival is also called Anni.

• It is one of the most important festivals of the Sumi Nagas.

NOTE

• Other Nagaland festivals: Hornbill Festival (the "festival of festivals", held in December), Moatsu (Ao tribe) and Sekrenyi (Angami tribe).

question: Which of the following award did Pandit Ravi Shankar win for four times?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Grammy Awards.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The legendary sitar maestro Pandit Ravi Shankar won the Grammy Award four times. (पंडित रवि शंकर — चार बार ग्रैमी पुरस्कार)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Pandit Ravi Shankar was a world-renowned sitar player who popularised Indian classical music globally, including collaborations with The Beatles' George Harrison and violinist Yehudi Menuhin.

• He was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1999, India's highest civilian honour.

NOTE

• He was the father of Grammy-winning musicians Anoushka Shankar and Norah Jones. The Grammy Awards are the highest honours in the global music industry.
